newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St Barbara says no decision on court action.
newsitem.headline: St Barbara says no decision on court action.

text.p: St Barbara Mines Ltd said on Wednesday the Supreme Court of Western Australia had heard the appeal by interests associated with shareholder Ross Atkins to block its merger with Mt Leyshon Mines Ltd.

St Barbara said the court had reserved its decision on Atkins' legal proceedings. The legal action was taken with a view to restraining St Barbara from despatching its formal takeover documents to fellow goldminer Mt Leyshon.
Atkins, jointly with former chairman Alan Birchmore, controls 47.2 percent of St Barbara. He was unseated as a director of St Barbara in October 1995.

St Barbara has said the offer would be 32 of its shares for each 10 Mt Leyshon shares. Normandy Mining Ltd, which controls 76 percent of Mt Leyshon, has not said whether it will accept the offer, which is subject to 75-percent acceptances.
St Barbara shares closed two cents higher at 71 cents on Monday while Mt Leyshon closed 10 cents weaker at A$2.10.

The two companies have a combined market capitalisation of about A$315 million at current prices. A successful merger would create a company with annual gold production of about 350,000 ounces and a resource base of about 4.8 million ounces.
